itinerary.cal: Washington Pass alpine season, roughly July through September. Bring an ice axe: the route crosses a steep snow couloir midway. Late in the season the basin camp has no running water and the col holds only hard snow.
itinerary.totalNote: A long alpine day on Burgundy Spire, best split with a camp in the basin below the spire: hike up the steep climbers' path from Highway 20 the first day, then climb the 15-pitch Corkscrew (rock to 5.6, a snow couloir up to about 50 degrees, then four pitches to 5.8), rappel the North Face to Burgundy Col and walk out.

days.title: Hike to the basin camp
days.objective: Reach a camp in the basin below Burgundy Spire
days.note: From the big pullout on Highway 20 east of Washington Pass (about 4,250 ft), drop through talus, cross Early Winters Creek on a log and climb the steep climbers' path up the forested rib left of Burgundy Creek. The basin camp sits near 6,500 ft, about two hours up; Burgundy Col at about 7,720 ft is the higher option.

schedule.label: Leave the highway pullout
schedule.detail: Cross Early Winters Creek on a log, then climb the rib north of Burgundy Creek.

schedule.label: Basin camp, about 6,500 ft
schedule.detail: Roughly two hours from the car.

days.title: Climb the Corkscrew, rappel, hike out
days.objective: Climb the Corkscrew to the 8,400 ft summit, rappel to the col and return to the car
days.note: Eight to ten pitches of rock up to 5.6 lead into a snow couloir of about 400 ft, up to 50 degrees, then four more pitches up to 5.8 reach the summit; the upper pitches finish on the west face near where the North Face route's ledge traverse arrives. Descend by rappelling the North Face line: from the summit block to a bolted anchor (a 60 m rope comes up about 10 ft short), more rappels to a ledge, a traverse, and further rappels over sandy terraces to Burgundy Col, about an hour and a half with ropes that like to snag. From the col it is about two hours back to the highway. Confirm where the route starts before you go: the base is not described in the sources found.

schedule.detail: About eight to ten pitches.

schedule.label: Snow couloir
schedule.detail: About 400 ft, up to 50 degrees; ice axe.

schedule.label: Upper pitches to 5.8
schedule.detail: Four pitches to the summit.

schedule.label: Rappel the North Face to Burgundy Col
schedule.detail: About 1.5 hours; a 70 m rope saves rappels.

schedule.label: Col to the car
schedule.detail: About 2 hours.

figureSources: Route make-up (pitches, couloir length and angle, grades, 1,500 ft, ice axe, descend the North Face) from the Mountain Project route page. Trailhead and basin/col elevations, the 2-hour basin time, the 1.5-hour rappel descent and the 2-hour col-to-car time from Steph Abegg's Burgundy Spire report (a North Face ascent). Summit 8,400 ft from Mountain Project and Abegg. Day 2 gainFt 1900 is NOT stated by a source: it is the difference between Abegg's 6,500 ft basin camp and the 8,400 ft summit, so treat it as derived. No source gives the Corkscrew's climbing time, start location or mileage.

itinerary.cal: Summer to early fall. A day trip needs no overnight permit; camping at Colchuck Lake from May 15 to October 31 needs an Enchantments overnight permit. Parking needs a Northwest Forest Pass or an America the Beautiful pass.
itinerary.totalNote: A long single day: the Colchuck Lake trail, a climbers' path to the cirque under the west face, eight-plus pitches of the West Face with this variation taking the place of the third pitch, a boulder move onto the balanced rock, then a short descent back to the base and the walk out. Car to car runs about 14.5 to 15.5 hours.

days.title: West Face of Colchuck Balanced Rock
days.objective: Climb the West Face with the Foot of Faith third-pitch variation and return to the car
days.note: Hike the Stuart Lake trailhead path to the north end of Colchuck Lake (about two hours), cross the outlet just below the dam, and follow a climbers' trail up the wooded slope into the cirque below the face, then scramble a third-class ramp to the base: three to four hours in all. The West Face runs about 850 ft and eight-plus pitches; this variation replaces the regular 5.9 third pitch, which stems a thin slabby corner to a treed ledge. Top out with a short boulder problem onto the balanced rock. Get down with one rappel of about 30 m east off a slung horn, or by downclimbing a gully of about 5.6, then scree or snow back around to the base, under an hour, and walk out in a bit under three hours.

days.title: West Face of Colchuck Balanced Rock
days.objective: Climb the West Face with the 1984 third-pitch variation and return to the car
days.note: Walk from the Stuart Lake trailhead to the north end of Colchuck Lake in about two hours, cross the outlet below the dam and take the climbers' trail up through timber to the cirque, finishing with a third-class ramp to the base; budget three to four hours. reason: Three searches for The Comb (Darrington) found no opened page describing Boomerang: the only listing (theCrag, which places it on Green Giant Buttress at 5.11a III) returned 403, and the Comb trip reports are on CascadeClimbers (blocked). The Green Giant Buttress pages opened (Mountain Project, Steph Abegg) list Dreamer and its neighbours but not Boomerang.

Desire on the Comb near Darrington appears only in a CascadeClimbers trip report (blocked) and a 403 theCrag listing. No opened page covers its approach, the Comb's own approach paths or its descent, so fewer than two usable sources.

itinerary.cal: Summer and early fall, once the approach creek crossings drop; parties have met high water at the stream crossings and running water on the route early in the season. Boulder River Wilderness.
itinerary.totalNote: A full single day near Darrington: about 3 miles and 1,500 ft of bushy approach to Green Giant Buttress, ten pitches of Dreamer (5.9, about 1,000 ft), nine or ten double-rope rappels back down the route, and the walk out.

days.title: Dreamer on Green Giant Buttress
days.objective: Climb Dreamer, rappel the route and walk out
days.note: From the end of the Clear Creek road southeast of Darrington, follow an old logging road extension and then an older mining road, cross a side fork of Copper Creek and follow the main fork to a set of three waterfalls. A small gully up and right into maples leads to a larger gully and the rock; scramble up and right to the staging area below the steep slabs. The approach is about 3 miles and 1,500 ft, roughly two hours, with some brush and a stream that can run high. Climb ten pitches of cracks and knobby face to 5.9, with gear to about 3 inches. Most parties rappel the route rather than walking off: nine or ten double-rope rappels with two 60 m ropes, about two hours, where flakes and trees catch ropes. The walk back to the road end takes about an hour and a quarter.

schedule.label: Road end to the base
schedule.detail: About 2 hours, roughly 3 miles and 1,500 ft.

schedule.label: Climb Dreamer
schedule.detail: Ten pitches, about 1,000 ft, 5.9.

schedule.label: Rappel the route
schedule.detail: Nine or ten double-rope rappels, about 2 hours.

schedule.label: Walk out
schedule.detail: About 1.25 hours to the road end.

Rappel-rather-than-walk-off advice from alpinedave; high creek crossings and bushwhack from chossclimbers. gainFt 1500 is the approach gain stated by Abegg; no source gives a car-to-car time, so hours is null.

itinerary.cal: Summer to early fall. A day trip needs no overnight permit; camping at Colchuck Lake or above it from May 15 to October 31 needs an Enchantments overnight permit. Parking needs a Northwest Forest Pass or an America the Beautiful pass.
itinerary.totalNote: A long single day on the northeast tower of Dragontail: the Colchuck Lake trail and the lower Aasgard Pass path to about 7,500 ft, seven pitches up the East Face of the NE Tower (5.8, about 1,000 ft, loose and not well cleaned), a gully descent with one rappel back to the Aasgard path, and the walk out past Colchuck Lake.

days.title: A Kidney for a Friend
days.objective: Climb the East Face of Dragontail's NE Tower and return to the car
days.note: Hike from the Stuart Lake trailhead to Colchuck Lake (4 miles and about 2,300 ft each way on trail), go around the lake and start up the Aasgard Pass path; roughly three hours from the car takes you to where climbers leave it. Above about 7,000 ft take the right-hand branch, cross the rockfall couloir near 7,500 ft and scramble a ledge past a few trees to the base of the small tower. Seven pitches (5.8 at most, then a 4th to 5.5 ridge and a third-class ledge system) reach the notch west of the summit tower, about five hours for the first party. The rock is loose and there are no fixed anchors. To descend, cross to the south side toward the Enchantment Snowfield, downclimb the gully on skier's right to a big tree, rappel about 30 m past a chimney, finish the gully and trend down and right to the Aasgard path. The walk from there back to the car is a bit under three hours.

itinerary.cal: Summer to early fall; it has also been climbed in winter. Bring an ice axe for snow on the approach and descent. Camping at Colchuck Lake or above it from May 15 to October 31 needs an Enchantments overnight permit; a day trip does not. Parking needs a Northwest Forest Pass or an America the Beautiful pass.
itinerary.totalNote: A long single day: the Colchuck Lake trail and the lower Aasgard Pass path to the toe of the buttress, about 2,000 ft of climbing (four loose pitches to 5.8 R, a chimney, then a long stretch of 4th class to 5.5 slabs best simul-climbed), a walk across the Enchantment snowfield to the summit, and down Aasgard Pass to the lake and the car.

days.title: Complete Northeast Buttress of Dragontail
days.objective: Climb the whole Northeast Buttress, tag the summit and descend Aasgard Pass
days.note: Walk the Stuart Lake trailhead path to Colchuck Lake (4 miles, about 2,300 ft on trail), round the lake and climb the Aasgard Pass path to the lowest point of the buttress; reaching the point where climbers leave that path takes about three hours. The first four pitches of cracks and chimneys (5.6 to 5.8 R) are poor rock where gear and holds can both pull. A better pitch leads to a chimney (5.7 to 5.8) that crosses the crest; above, the rock improves into a long run of 4th class to easy 5th slab that most parties simul-climb. The route tops out in the towers short of the true summit; drop to the snowfield and hike to the top. Descend Aasgard Pass, loose and steep, back to Colchuck Lake; from the base of the face the walk to the car took a bit under three hours on a neighbouring route.

schedule.label: Summit

schedule.label: Descend Aasgard Pass and hike out
